doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First trip to the West Coast and the Swing Club in Hollywood
summary: The reformed big band toured west in 1942 and played Billy Berg's Swing Club, briefly with Buddy Rich.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: In early 1942 you reformed the big band.
Yes, that’s right. That’s right, yeah, yeah. That’s right.
Okay, that’s sort of, well, a question, a statement, I don’t know.
Then you toured in the summer and went on a western swing, which landed you in Los Angeles [California].
Was that your first trip to the West Coast?
Yep, first trip to the West Coast ever.
And you played in the Swing Club in Hollywood. Any impressions of the music scene in the West Coast at that time?

No, it was during the war, you know, and the only thing I do remember, I had Buddy Rich on drums for a couple of weeks while he was awaiting his greetings. [laughter] But beyond that, no, I don’t remember anything. You know, naturally there were sailors and soldiers from time to time, but other than that the clientele was quite ordinary, the usual jazz lover or music lover. It was a nice room to work in, and the owner of the club was a nice guy to work for, Billy Berg [phonetic].
